AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: The latter are inhabited by over 15 million people, i.e. 39.5% of Polish population, including about 5 million rural residents in the Podlaskie voivodeship. The incidence of obesity is associated with increased prevalence of obesity-related conditions. The conducted studies do not confirm the efficacy of conservative treatment obesity, but show that bariatric procedures produce the best long-term results.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: The aim of the study was to present the effects of bariatric obesity treatment (LAGB, SG, RYGB) on body mass index (BMI), selected diabetes control parameters, dyslipidemia, hepatic and renal enzymes, blood count, and hypertension control.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: A total of 100 consecutive patients from rural areas, qualified for bariatric procedures. Most patients (69.07%) in the study group underwent SG, 11.34% LAGB, and 19.59% RYGB. Comorbidities included hypertension (35%), type 2 diabetes (52%), and hyperlipidemia (15%). Glucose, insulin, HbA1C, alanine and aspartate aminotransferase, bilirubin, total and fraction cholesterol, creatinine, urea, uric acid, CRP levels as well as blood count and blood pressure values were assessed prior to surgery and during follow-up visits 3 and 6 months after the procedure. BMI was assessed; %EWL and %EBMIL.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: A consistent, significant decrease in BMI was observed 3 months (39.31±4.70) and 6 months (35.74±4.52) after surgery. The largest BMI reduction following 6-month follow up was observed for SG (12.29%), and the smallest BMI reduction was observed for LAGB (9.02%).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: We found an improvement in the general health status of patients as well as normalization of metabolic parameters (glucose, cholesterol, triglycerides, hepatic enzymes).
